doc_verification.detail: Reachability PASS via MCP web reader (WebFetch domain_blocked for api.qdrant.tech/docs.qdrant.tech; reader fetched full page). Versioned page https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/collections/delete-collection live, shows v1.18.x = target 1.18.0 major.minor. Versioned API ref confirms endpoint shape: param 'Name of the collection to delete', description 'Drops the specified collection and all associated data in it.', ONLY a 200 response documented (no 404), result:boolean with false semantics undocumented (example shows result:true). The alias-equivalence premise of the script ('all queries identically via alias') is supported ONLY by the current-only concept doc (qdrant.tech/documentation/manage-data/collections/, fetched live: 'Aliases are additional names for existing collections. All queries to the collection can also be done identically, using an alias instead of the collection name.'), which per raw_knowledge.md provenance is corroborative current-site content, not the versioned contract; the versioned spec is silent on aliases for both GET and DELETE /collections/{name}. Note: raw_knowledge.md line 131 claims 'deleting non-existent collection -> 404' but the versioned API ref documents only 200 for this endpoint — that 404 claim is not in the fetched spec. Content consistency PARTIAL for these reasons. Endpoint precision PASS: endpoint_registry 'collections+delete' matches script path and source_url.

http_semantics.note: Deleting a name absent from the collections map (here an alias that resolves for GET) returns HTTP 200 + status:ok with the not-deleted state expressed only as body flag result:false — no error code, no 4xx. A client that keys on HTTP status (as the script did) reads success.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: candidates.jsonl constraint_id is EMPTY (mechanical extraction gap); grounding recovered from script header (debate_logs/semantic_collections_delete_006.py line 7: constraint_ids: qdrant_bc_collection_delete_isolation_001). Contract text (structured_contract.json behavioral_contracts): description 'deleting a collection removes its points; other collections unaffected', expected_behavior 'deleted collection GET => 404; other collection count unchanged', related_endpoints [collections+delete, collections+get, points+count], source_url v-1-18-x delete-collection. Directly matching state_invariant qdrant_inv_collection_gone_after_delete_001: 'after successful delete, GET collection returns 404', assertion 'delete => 200 THEN collections+get => 404'.
contract_grounding.note: At the HTTP-status reading the assertion is literally violated: DELETE => 200, subsequent GET on the same resource (real name) => 200, not 404. Two qualifications the auditor must weigh: (1) the deleted spelling was an ALIAS, and the versioned spec param says 'Name of the collection to delete' without addressing aliases — the 'aliases work identically' premise rests on the current-only concept doc; under that doc reading, delete-via-alias should have deleted the underlying collection and GET => 404; (2) the response body result:false is the server's own non-deletion signal, so 'success reported' holds at the HTTP envelope level only. Not a silent-accept ambiguity: violates=true is asserted at the layer the invariant is worded in (status codes).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: DELETE /collections/{name} -> src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:160 delete_collection (passes RAW path name) -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::DeleteCollection) -> collection_meta_ops.rs:78 -> Toc::delete_collection (:211) -> collections.remove(raw_name): alias not in map -> result=false -> Ok(false) -> helpers.rs process_response -> HTTP 200 + result:false; underlying collection untouched. GET /collections/{name} -> collections_api.rs:59 -> Toc::get_collection_unchecked (mod.rs:368) -> resolve_name (mod.rs:407) resolves alias->real name -> 200 on real collection. Asymmetry confirmed: resolve_name is called on the read path and never on the delete path. Also noted: delete of a REAL collection calls alias_persistence.remove_collection (meta_ops :217-220) which strips that collection's aliases — the alias subsystem is only consulted as a victim of real-name delete, never as an input name resolver for delete.
source_grounding.outcome_note: The 200+result:false no-op is explicit intentional code (Ok(result) with result=false for any name absent from the collections map — including aliases and never-existing names; no 404 mapping exists anywhere on this path). At the same time the alias-resolution step that the read path performs (resolve_name) is demonstrably absent from the delete path, which is what makes delete-via-alias a silent no-op instead of either deleting the underlying collection (concept-doc 'all queries identically' reading) or signaling 404 (raw_knowledge state note). Both facts are in source; which framing defeats or sustains the defect claim is the auditor's call.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by_design reading: server deliberately reports not-deleted via body result:false under HTTP 200 for any unmapped name; combined with the versioned spec being silent on aliases for DELETE, a 'works as coded, spec does not promise alias resolution on delete' defense is available. Against it stands the concept-doc sentence 'All queries to the collection can also be done identically, using an alias instead of the collection name' (current-only, corroborative) and the documented-only-200 response that leaves no 4xx channel for this case. Undecided here — auditor's judgment.
